chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is the status of the two rak'ahs before the dawn prayer?' He said: 'Before the rising of the dawn (sun). When the dawn rises, the time for the dawn prayer has entered.'
And from him from Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

I read in a man's letter to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Are the two rak'ahs before the dawn prayer part of the night prayer or the day prayer? And at what time should I pray them?' He wrote in his own hand: 'Include them in the night prayer as an addition (hashw).'

key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: The rising of the sun (end of Fajr time)

ai.seo_question: When should the two sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr be prayed and are they part of night prayer?
ai.summary: These narrations from al-Tahdhib clarify that the two sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr are classified as part of Salat al-Layl (night prayer) added as an appendage, to be performed before the true dawn (Fajr al-Sadiq) enters. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of night worship into the early morning, distinguishing the voluntary pre-Fajr prayer from the obligatory Fajr prayer which begins with the appearance of true dawn.
